items.title: Bitcoin tumbles below $76,000 as post-election stock rally fades
items.summary:
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) tumbled below $76,000 on Thursday as investors moved out of riskier assets amid a broad sell-off in US stocks that threatened to erase the previous day's post-election rally.

The world's largest cryptocurrency fell 5% Thursday, reversing a sharp rebound Wednesday that had lifted bitcoin above $80,000 as investors cheered midterm election results showing Democrats swept both chambers of Congress. [...] Bitcoin's latest slide follows a warning from digital asset research firm K33 earlier this week that unusually thin trading activity and rising use of leverage set up bitcoin for sharp price swings following midterm results.

Bitcoin's retreat also underscored of the crypto market's lingering fragility following $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, which rattled crypto prices last week. [...] On the other hand, others see a silver lining for bitcoin post-midterms. Sean Farrell, Fundstrat's head of digital assets, argued in a Wednesday afternoon note to clients that the decisive Democratic victory in Congress could strengthen the largest cryptocurrency's appeal as a hedge against larger federal deficits.

Representation of Bitcoin cryptocurrency in this illustration taken September 10, 2025. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic
